submission.natural_language_explanation: A recent-window mixing head: it splits its attention between itself and the 1-3 tokens before it (mean weights 0.21/0.24/0.19/0.11 at lags 0-3 in prose), so its write leaves its mean write whenever that little window holds something other than an ordinary whole word. It is strongly active (0.5-1.0 of max) at a text's 2nd token when the 1st token is a bracket or bracket-like delimiter ('(', ')', '[', ']', '{', '}', '『', '「', '<', or a bracketed item marker such as '(1)', '(Note)', '[Update]') or when the opening word is split by the tokenizer into several pieces ('H'+'ym'+'en'+'aea', 'Jose'+'f', 'Dr'+'unk', ' M'+'oser', 'Sch'+'olars'); the same trigger is weak (0.25-0.45 of max) at tokens 3-6 and sinks below the active line deeper in ordinary prose, so predict inactive any text that opens with 'The' (or 'It', 'They', 'There', 'Our', 'He', 'She', 'We') plus a common lowercase word and then runs on as plain prose with no bracket, quote, digit, capitalised name or tokenizer-split word ('A'/'An' plus a noun is borderline, about 0.3 of max).

rival_explanations: Text-start (positional) head: its write departs from the mean at the first two or three tokens of any text whatever they contain, an attention-sink or window-start effect, so 'The house is near the park' should peak as high as '(8) is a number' and the brackets in the top examples are incidental.

Position-free rarity head: it fires wherever its window holds a low-frequency token, any rare word, digit or punctuation including '.' and ',', at the same strength deep inside a text as at token 2, with no special role for brackets or word fragments.

Capitalised-name detector: since PROPN tokens fire far more often than average (754/26253 active, mean strength 0.34 against 0.19 overall) and person-name tokens average 0.54, the head tracks capitalised name pieces and should fire on a capitalised name anywhere in a text but not on brackets, digits or code punctuation.
